errors.text: The proposed Mg65Al15Cr10Fe5Ni5 composition replaces the target MgAlTiVFeCo system and omits Ti, V, and Co, which are central to the target BCC precursor and barrier-phase chemistry.

It predicts 900 °C as optimal and treats 1000 °C as volatility-limited, directly opposing the target result that SPS at 1000 °C gives the best density, hardness, oxidation resistance, and corrosion resistance.

The claim that a Mg-rich alloy with Fe, Ni, and Cr will form an entropy-stabilized single FCC/BCC phase is unsupported by the cited Fe/Ni-based HEA literature and ignores the restricted mutual solubilities and strong intermetallic-forming tendencies in Mg-rich systems.

The proposed Al2O3/Cr2O3 barrier mechanism does not recover the target uniformly distributed AlV2O4, FeAl2O4, and FeTiO3 barrier phases, passive-film behavior, or biphasic parabolic oxidation mechanism.

The assertion that Al and Cr preferentially oxidize over Mg is not established and is chemically questionable for a Mg-rich alloy, where MgO formation and Mg-driven degradation are likely to dominate.
Quantitative predictions of greater than 98% density at 900 °C, greater than 150 HV hardness, and a 50% corrosion-current reduction have no direct supporting evidence.
